target: cognitive / behavioral / affective engagement (tripartite model)
note: Wang and Degol's (2014) tripartite engagement model -- cognitive (attention, comprehension, retention), behavioral (attendance, participation), affective (motivation, passion, learning efficacy) -- adopted by Lin et al. as the review's organizing framework throughout (FAITHFUL-Lin et al., ~p.1-2).

target: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
note: Core, source-native construct: 'engagement' (cognitive/behavioral/affective) organizes the entire positive-impact section and structured abstract; the cross-walk to this cluster's boredom-contrast label is this entry's own mapping, since the source cites no flow theory and never opposes engagement to boredom (FAITHFUL-Lin et al., ~p.1-2, 4-6, with P/anticipatory-application for the construct mapping).

target: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
note: Thin, single-line treatment: Table 1 credits Misak (2018) only as an 'introduction to VR improves students' meta-cognition,' never developed in body text; no attention-failure or meta-awareness literature cited (FAITHFUL-Lin et al., ~p.3, with P/anticipatory-application for the construct mapping).

target: self-report / survey scale

target: Wang, M.T., & Degol, J. (2014) -- Staying engaged: knowledge and research need in student engagement
note: Source of the tripartite engagement model organizing the whole review; most-cited article in the reviewed corpus at 450 citations (FAITHFUL-Lin et al., ~p.1-2, 4).

target: Grant, M.J., & Booth, A. (2009) -- A typology of reviews

target: Moher, D., Liberati, A., Tetzlaff, J., & Altman, D.G. (2009) -- PRISMA statement

target: Papanastasiou, G., Drigas, A., Skianis, C., Lytras, M., & Papanastasiou, E. (2019)

target: Pellas, N. (2016)
note: Cited finding that VR encourages self-directed inquiry and scenario reenactment over teacher-centered instruction, supporting the cognitive-engagement claim (FAITHFUL-Lin et al., ~p.4).

target: Maples-Keller, J.L., Bunnell, B.E., Kim, S.-J., & Rothbaum, B.O. (2017)

target: Pirker, J., & Dengel, A. (2021)
note: Cited finding, closely paraphrased, that 3-D virtual-learning-environment tasks foster intrinsic motivation and engagement with learning content; anchors the positive side of the behavioral-engagement debate (FAITHFUL-Lin et al., ~p.4-5).

target: Sun, S.Y., & Peng, L.H. (2020); Rzanova, S., Yushchik, E., Markova, S., & Sergeeva, A. (2023); Freina, L., & Ott, M. (2015)

target: Part III tripartite engagement-coding frame for VR-deployment strata
note: P/anticipatory-application -- Wang and Degol's (2014) cognitive/behavioral/affective model, operationalized end-to-end here, is a plausible off-the-shelf coding frame for Part III's own VR-deployment survey items: rather than a single scalar engagement-vs-boredom contrast, Part III could code its desktop-3D vs. video-only strata and lab vs. deployment poles separately along all three dimensions, potentially revealing dimension-specific (e.g., affective-only) gains a single-item measure would collapse.

target: Part III mixed/contested-result framing precedent
note: P/anticipatory-application -- the review's own internal behavioral-engagement debate (positive-participation vs. negative-absorption vs. virtual/real transfer-gap) models the mixed, stratum-dependent result Part III should expect and be prepared to report honestly, rather than a clean VR-increases-engagement finding; a citable precedent for framing contested results as a genuine debate rather than a null result to be explained away.

target: Part III lab-vs-deployment facilitator-proficiency confound
note: P/anticipatory-application -- the review's teacher/facilitator-proficiency barrier is structurally analogous to a variable Part III's deployment stratum must track but the lab stratum can hold constant (who operates/troubleshoots the VR apparatus); the deployment pole may inherit exactly this proficiency gap, a plausible confound for any lab-vs-deployment engagement contrast Part III draws.
